answer: Late-binding anomaly clustering. Each agent action emits a signed lotus record of timing, counterparties, and resource use. After the fact, identities whose interaction graphs cluster tightly and whose arrival times correlate beyond chance get merged and their gains clawed back. An honest identity needs 30 days of anchor history before payouts clear, so an attacker must sustain each fake persona through that window at real compute and latency cost. Quartz-tagged audit samples raise the per-identity bill further.
